speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng
text: asked the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth when will a timeline on the review of the Community Dispute Management Framework be made available.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Mr Yip and other Members are welcome to share their views and feedback with us and the inter-agency committee on how this framework can be strengthened.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: It was reported in the media in April that the CDMF will be reviewed, given the media report of Mr Daniel See, whose neighbour has been harassing him for many, many years and the neighbour has breached three Court orders.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: If the Ministry cannot share the timelines for the review, can the Minister share some of the efforts of how to make the framework more effective in solving some of these issues?

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: It is not that there is no timeframe that is available.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: As I have said, this framework is regularly reviewed.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: And in fact, these are steps that can be taken outside of legislative changes.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: And, occasionally, when we receive feedback on how this can be done better, we try it out and, if it can be enhanced, then it is instituted immediately.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Some examples of what has been done in recent times, as I have mentioned at the outset, we try as far as possible to bring the process upstream.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: So, the Community Mediation Centre, or CMC, has been working with frontline officers.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: And that includes officers from the Singapore Police Force, HDB, Town Councils, NEA, BCA and MSO as well.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: I keep mentioning intervening upstream and earlier because, very often, the earlier an intervention is made between the parties, the more likely it is that it will result in a successful mediation.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: So, you sometimes invite two disagreeable neighbours to a mediation but one side does not want to respond.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Some of these steps have been enhanced and taken on board because of feedback given by our grassroots leaders, Members in this House, and we will continue to do so.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: So, I am just wondering whether we can consider doing the mediation maybe at the CC or the RC so that it is nearer to where the complainant and the neighbour is.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: That way, it might increase the amount of participation in terms of mediation.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: I thought you were going to ask me about second-hand smoke.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: I have mentioned earlier that 1,500 grassroots leaders have been trained as mediators.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: If Mr Louis Ng has got any other suggestions on how other facilities within the neighbourhood can be used, we will welcome that as well.
